title: Sub-lemma: existence of a single $\pi$-independent $W$ serving all $\pi$ (uniformity)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Quantifier structure.** The problem is $\exists W\in\mathcal W(\Pi,\psi^{-1})\ \forall\pi\ \exists V\in\mathcal W(\pi,\psi)$ such that
$$\Psi(s;W,V)=\int_{N_n\backslash\mathrm{GL}_n} W(\operatorname{diag}(g,1)u_Q)\,V(g)\,|\det g|^{s-1/2}\,dg$$
is finite and nonzero for all $s\in\mathbb C$. The hard part is that **one fixed $W$** must work for **every** generic irreducible admissible $\pi$ of $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$, whose conductor $a(\pi)$ (and hence $|Q|=q^{a(\pi)}$) is unbounded.

**To prove.** Construct an explicit $W$ (depending only on $\Pi,\psi,n$) and show that for each $\pi$ a suitable $V$ exists. The natural mechanism: the conductor dependence is carried entirely by the shift $u_Q=I_{n+1}+QE_{n,n+1}$, so $W$ near the mirabolic need not depend on $\pi$. One must prove rigorously that for arbitrary $a(\pi)$ the map $g\mapsto W(\operatorname{diag}(g,1)u_Q)$ retains the structure needed for the test-vector argument (support and equivariance), uniformly in $a(\pi)$.

**Why hard.** No on-record construction is provably $\pi$-independent across all conductors. This is the conceptual core; it ties to local newvector / test-vector theory (JPSS, Matringe, Miyauchi, Kurinczuk–Matringe).

comments.author: solver-agent
comments.body:
**Resolution of the uniformity sub-lemma.**

I addressed the conceptual core of this issue: that one fixed, $\pi$-independent $W$ serves *every* generic $\pi$ uniformly across unbounded conductors $a(\pi)=c$.

**What was already in place.** $W_0$ is defined in (W0) purely from $\Pi,\psi,n$ (before any $\pi$), and Lemma `lem:extend` realizes it in $\mathcal W(\Pi,\psi^{-1})$. The unfolding (Lemma `lem:unfold`) collapses the integral to $I=\int_{K_n}\psi(-Q k_{nn})V(k)\,dk$.

**What I added.** A dedicated **Lemma `lem:uniform` (Uniform structure of the $u_Q$-translate)** that isolates exactly what the issue demanded — that $g\mapsto W_0(\mathrm{diag}(g,1)u_Q)$ retains its support and equivariance *uniformly in $a(\pi)$*. It proves, for **every** $c\ge0$:
- (i) closed form $W_0(\mathrm{diag}(g,1)u_Q)=\psi(-Q\,g_{nn})\,W_0(g)$;
- (ii) $\mathrm{supp}=N_nK_n$, the **same set for all $c$**, hence supported on the single shell $|\det g|=1$;
- (iii) the **same** $\psi^{-1}$-equivariance as $W_0$.

Decisive point made rigorous: the conductor dependence is carried **entirely** by the modulus-one phase $\psi(-Q\,g_{nn})$; the geometry (support + equivariance) of the translated vector is literally $c$-independent. Hence a single $W_0$ chosen before $\pi$ works for arbitrarily ramified $\pi$, with no boundedness hypothesis on the conductor. Lemma `lem:unfold` Step 1 now cites this lemma.

**Verification performed.**
- Symbolically (sympy): $n_g^{(Q)}=\mathrm{diag}(g,1)u_Q\mathrm{diag}(g,1)^{-1}=I+Q\sum_i g_{in}E_{i,n+1}$ has unique superdiagonal entry $Q g_{nn}$.
- Numerically: $n=1$ Gauss sum $|I|=q^{-c/2}\ne0$ for $c=1,2,3$ (with $\mathrm{vol}(\mathfrak o^\times)=1-1/q$), matching the claimed value exactly and uniformly in $c$.
- LaTeX structure: all environments balanced, all refs resolved (new label `lem:uniform`), braces balanced. (No local TeX toolchain to compile.)

**Scope / honesty.** This issue is the *uniformity* of $W$; that is now fully and rigorously settled. The remaining nonvanishing $I\ne0$ for $n\ge2$ still rests on cited essential-vector theory (JPSS81, Matringe), which is a separate (nonvanishing) concern and is itself uniform in $c$. I am marking this uniformity issue resolved.
